I think we've all seen some laziness from the game's industry but Activison had to take it a step further. While I do consider myself a fan of the Prototype series I feel ripped off to be honest.

Performance

The performance hasn't really been improved over the last gen counterparts. The FPS is still oddly locked at 30fps when realisitcally and technlogically it could push 60fps without even breaking a sweat. This applies for both Prototype 1 HD and Prototype 2 HD.

Here's a Digital Foundry video that takes a look at the frame rate. https://youtu.be/UGqkhkS4fqI

This is unacceptable a game like Prototype should rightly run at 60fps.

Its also unaccptable when the marketing for the game made a point that the frame rate had improved. Which is obviously hadn't and as seen in the above video its gotten worse.

Actual Upgrades?

Apart from being in 1080p there's litterally nothing else that has been improved. Again this means that the game should be running at 60fps at least.

Unknown Developers

We also have no idea who "Developed" (I think you know why I used quotation marks here) this port either. Usually we'd see their logos at the begging of the game but instead Radical the developers of the original games are listed even though Radical themselves had nothing to do with this port. Considering that Radical Entertainment's staff were laid off and the people left there became support for bigger titles.

Also I found this comment on EuroGamer which I found interesting. http://i.imgur.com/g9rpSi4.png Although it should be noted that there's no way to verify if this person did indeed work at RadicalEntertainment.

I think its obvious why Activison choose to keep the identity of the developers a secret. They don't want the mess that Arkham Knight on PC had with Iron Galaxy.

Price

At £40 its very expensive for a remaster, and I advise it be avoided. Like your not getting a better experience.

Release date wrong for PS4?

Also it should be noted that the game was supposed to be released this past Tuesday but PS4 owners had to wait until the day after to be able to play it. Another example of false advertising, Activison should have known about PS4's Wednesday store updates but they didn't account for that in their marketing.

Bottom Line

Bottom line is that they released this without any thought as to what the term "Remaster" means. We've got a game that was fasley advertised, barely had improvements over the original and is very overpriced for what we got. Here's hoping that the frame rate gets boosted in a patch but I wouldn't hold my breath.

To me it seems like this game was released ahead of the Xbox One Backwards compatability program, and Activison will make sure that the original X360 releases of both games will not be compatible with it.
